# Overview

`MIMSTEM` implements three marginal interventional multi-state mediation
estimators for time-to-event mediators:

- `mims_tem()` for one time-to-event mediator;
- `mims_s2tem_ge()` for overall effects with two sequential time-to-event mediators;
- `mims_s2tem_pe()` for path-specific decomposition with two sequential time-to-event mediators.

The package preserves the estimands and numerical conventions used by the
validated dissertation estimators. The recommended workflow is to validate the
data and point estimates first, inspect diagnostics, and only then request the
computationally intensive bootstrap.

# Required data structure

For MIMS-TEM, the subject-level data frame contains `A`, `t_out`, `d_out`
(or `yevent`), `t_med`, `d_med`, and the baseline covariates named in `basec`.

For MIMS-S2TEM-GE and MIMS-S2TEM-PE, the corresponding mediator columns are
`t_med1`, `d_med1`, `t_med2`, and `d_med2`. Exposure `A` must be coded 0/1.
The package expects one row per subject.

Two synthetic data files are installed for workflow demonstrations. They are
not dissertation empirical data.

```{r example-data}
library(MIMSTEM)

tem_dat <- utils::read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "mims_example_tem.csv", package = "MIMSTEM")
)

s2_dat <- utils::read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "mims_example_s2tem.csv", package = "MIMSTEM")
)

names(tem_dat)
names(s2_dat)
```

# MIMS-TEM

Start with point estimation.

```{r tem-point}
fit_tem <- mims_tem(
  dat = tem_dat,
  tau = c(2, 4, 6),
  basec = c("age", "sex"),
  bootstrap = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

summary(fit_tem)
coef(fit_tem, tau = 6)
```

After checking the data coding and model diagnostics, bootstrap inference can
be requested. The dissertation-standard default is ordinary individual-level
nonparametric resampling with bootstrap standard errors and Wald confidence
intervals.

```{r tem-bootstrap}
fit_tem_boot <- mims_tem(
  dat = tem_dat,
  tau = c(2, 4, 6),
  basec = c("age", "sex"),
  bootstrap = TRUE,
  B = 200,
  seed = 2026,
  stratified = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

summary(fit_tem_boot, tau = 6)
confint(fit_tem_boot, tau = 6)
```

# MIMS-S2TEM-GE

MIMS-S2TEM-GE estimates total, direct, and overall indirect effects for the
complete sequential mediator process.

```{r ge-point}
fit_ge <- mims_s2tem_ge(
  dat = s2_dat,
  tau = c(2, 4, 6),
  basec = c("age", "sex"),
  bootstrap = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

summary(fit_ge, tau = 6)
fit_ge$point
```

The risk endpoints are `psi00`, `psi10`, and `psi11`, with

`DE = psi10 - psi00`,

`IE = psi11 - psi10`, and

`TE = psi11 - psi00`.

# MIMS-S2TEM-PE

MIMS-S2TEM-PE retains the GE endpoints and introduces two intermediate
counterfactual risks. The frozen switch order is `(zY, z2, z1, z12)`:

`psi0000 -> psi1000 -> psi1100 -> psi1110 -> psi1111`.

The primary analysis uses rank-preserving coupling for the two counterfactual
copies of the first mediator and the `t2_overrides` mixed-history rule.

```{r pe-point}
fit_pe <- mims_s2tem_pe(
  dat = s2_dat,
  tau = c(2, 4, 6),
  basec = c("age", "sex"),
  bootstrap = FALSE,
  primary_rule = "t2_overrides",
  verbose = FALSE
)

summary(fit_pe, tau = 6)
fit_pe$point
```

The main PE effects are

- `DE = psi1000 - psi0000`;
- `P_A_T2_Y = psi1100 - psi1000`;
- `P_A_T1_Y = psi1110 - psi1100`;
- `P_A_T1_T2_Y = psi1111 - psi1110`;
- `TE = psi1111 - psi0000`.

The overall indirect effect remains available in `fit_pe$point$IE_total` and
satisfies

`IE_total = P_A_T2_Y + P_A_T1_Y + P_A_T1_T2_Y`.

# GE/PE consistency

When GE and PE are fitted to the same data using the same settings, the shared
endpoints should agree up to numerical tolerance.

```{r endpoint-checks}
max(abs(fit_pe$point$psi0000 - fit_ge$point$psi00))
max(abs(fit_pe$point$psi1000 - fit_ge$point$psi10))
max(abs(fit_pe$point$psi1111 - fit_ge$point$psi11))

max(abs(
  fit_pe$point$IE_total -
    fit_pe$point$P_A_T2_Y -
    fit_pe$point$P_A_T1_Y -
    fit_pe$point$P_A_T1_T2_Y
))
```

# Results and diagnostics

All public estimators return an object inheriting from `mims_fit`.

```{r result-access}
fit_pe$point
fit_pe$endpoints
fit_pe$effects
fit_pe$diagnostics
fit_pe$settings

as.data.frame(fit_pe)
coef(fit_pe, tau = 6)
confint(fit_pe, tau = 6)
plot(fit_pe)
```

Cox-model warnings and path-kernel clipping diagnostics should be inspected,
not automatically suppressed. A numerically produced estimate does not by
itself establish the assumptions required for causal interpretation.

# Reproducibility checklist

For a reproducible analysis, record the package version, evaluation times,
baseline covariates, exposure contrast, `EMint`, S2TEM grid settings, PE
mixed-history rule, bootstrap replicate count, bootstrap seed, and resampling
scheme.

```{r reproducibility}
packageVersion("MIMSTEM")
fit_pe$settings
```
